title: Experience Deploying Containerized GenAI Services at an HPC Center
problem: GenAI workloads require containerized services (inference servers, databases, APIs) designed for cloud. Deploying these at HPC centers requires integrating cloud practices with traditional HPC infrastructure.
motivation: GenAI adoption increasing; HPC centers need to support LLM inference and related workloads. Container technology bridges HPC and cloud but deployment patterns, tooling, and best practices remain immature.
method: The approach packages GenAI software—specifically a vLLM inference server for running Llama models—into containers (portable bundles containing all code and dependencies). These same containers are deployed on both traditional HPC systems and Kubernetes (cloud-style infrastructure management) using multiple container runtimes (software that executes containers). By testing which runtimes work on both platforms, they show their containerized GenAI workloads can run on either HPC or Kubernetes infrastructure.
key_novelty: This is the first practical demonstration that containerized GenAI workloads can run on both Kubernetes and HPC systems using container runtimes compatible with both platforms.
contributions: Practical experience deploying GenAI services at HPC center
Converged computing architecture bridging HPC and Kubernetes
Evaluation of Llama LLM inference with vLLM across platforms
Container runtime compatibility assessment for HPC environment
limitations: Abstract only; no performance metrics or scaling results; limited to single LLM (Llama); generalization to other GenAI services unclear.
